one_line: Stable, shared review previews where agents can inspect, anchor, and resolve visual feedback in context.
what_it_does: Publishes a stable preview URL and attaches selector, viewport, version, source/style context, and threaded feedback so an agent and reviewer can collaborate on the same build.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP materially changes the review loop by exposing exact live comment context, viewport changes, CSS inspection, and thread actions in the same browser state; generic UI driving would be substantially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and transcript describe 13 same-tab tools for reading comments, focusing elements, switching to 390px, reading CSS, and posting fixes.
Stable URL preserves review state across published versions.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent end-to-end publish, annotate, inspect, fix, republish, and resolve workflow with detailed transcript evidence, though direct live observation is absent.
execution_evidence: 149-second video transcript describes the full central workflow.
Public repository and demo link are reported.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete, recurring developer-review communication problem for teams sharing visual feedback, with a credible reduction in translation and breakpoint ambiguity.
impact_evidence: Description identifies screenshot-and-sentence handoff friction.
Workflow keeps feedback attached to element, viewport, and version.
creativity_rationale: The same-tab human-reviewer/agent collaboration model and versioned, spatially anchored feedback are a fresh synthesis pursued beyond a generic comment tool.

usability_note: The described click-to-anchor and stable-link flow is straightforward for reviewers.
red_flags: No direct image inspection was possible because the vision service hit an open-file limit.
standouts: Strong WebMCP-specific same-tab collaboration and precise visual context capture.
advance_reason: Strong leverage and unusually complete end-to-end evidence.
